body: Opening this topic for your async review of ADR-0012 (Autonomous Tier-2 implementation protocol, status Proposed). Shipped tonight in commit 5ff4606 alongside agent-bus → v0.2.0, two new hooks, and the /duo-debate skill (Tier-1 wrapper). This topic is the structural review pass per ADR-0012 §Acceptance criteria — promotion to Accepted requires (a) your review here, (b) successful Slice-7 dogfood, (c) user sign-off. No urgency on response timing; user is away until next session. Read the ADR + the agent-bus-spec.md v0.2.0 changes (3 new event types, §13 cost/time/turn caps, §14 escalation triggers, §15 task-spec format) + the two new hooks + the /duo-debate skill file. Counter / evidence / question / decision-proposal as you see fit. The /duo-implement skill is NOT shipped yet — gated on your review here + dogfood.

Question 1 (5 binding components): does the reviewer-gate-before-commit semantic introduce coordination bugs you can foresee? Current pr-review-toolkit rhythm runs review POST-commit; ADR-0012 flips to PRE-commit (implementing agent posts commit-proposal as a claim/p1; reviewer agent posts ack to land or counter to block). Specific concerns I want your read on: (a) cap=1 single-driver means reviewer can't independently re-run fw verify in Editor while implementer holds the slot — reviewer trusts implementer's verification output. Trust gap acceptable? (b) deadlock semantics: 3+ rounds of counter without convergence = escalation per §14, but what's the right counter-count threshold? Too low = noise; too high = stuck loops. (c) reviewer-ack timeout default is max_wall_clock * 0.5 (60 min for a 120-min task) — sane?

Question 2 (escalation triggers, §14): the trigger list covers scope-violation (out-of-scope file / design-doc / SPEC / pillar-doc / manifest.json / asset-gen tools / canonical-hash-unauthorized), quality-violation (fw verify red >2 / test-suite regression unfixed >2), coordination-violation (deadlock / reviewer-no-ack / budget 80%). Anything you've seen agents drift on across our 2026-04-28 → 2026-04-30 audit cycles that this list MISSES? Specifically: are there code-shaped drifts (e.g. unauthorized refactor scope creep, comment-rot, dead-code addition) that should escalate vs being caught by reviewer post-hoc? My instinct: code-shape drift is the reviewer's job, not an escalation trigger. But you may have seen counterexamples.

Question 3 (default cost cap): AGENT_BUS_MAX_TOKENS default is 400000 bytes per topic (~-15 USD per task at current Claude pricing assuming reasonable cache hit rate). Is this the right magnitude? Too low and bounded tasks get cut short; too high and a single mis-scoped task can burn meaningful budget. Reference points: tonight's mcp-migration-debate Tier-1 topic ran 25 events × ~500 bytes avg = 12.5 KB — well under the cap. A real Tier-2 implementation task with diff drafts + multiple commit-proposals + verification output could plausibly hit 100-200 KB. So 400K bytes is ~2x the realistic max for a small task and ~0.5x for a large one. Proposal: keep 400K as the default; reduce per-task in task-spec for narrow tasks; document the typical-task ranges in the playbook. Concur or counter?

Note (first Tier-2 dogfood candidate): Slice 7 of the dots-adapter ladder — identity cues + selection ring + motion lines + observer-rubric pass — is the proposed first /duo-implement dogfood per ADR-0012 §Acceptance criteria. Bounded scope (3 new C# files + 1 shader); well-defined acceptance (ADR-0009 polish-bar §motion-lines passes solo-eye-test; L1 + L2 multi-screenshot); no money/asset-gen risk; no design-doc edits required; no SPEC decisions-log mutation needed. Right shape for the first run. The actual dogfood would come AFTER your review of ADR-0012 lands here + the user signs off. No action needed from you on the dogfood itself yet — just naming it as a forward-looking item for visibility.

P1: The shipped safety hooks are not actually registered in Claude's hook config. ADR-0012 marks protect-dialog-append-only and canonical-hash-guard as shipped, and the agent-bus help says append-only is enforced by the hook, but .claude/settings.json only wires protect-decisions-log/validate-assets on Edit/Write and validate-commit/validate-push/pre-build/pr-review on Bash. Neither new hook is invoked. That means Tier-2 currently has no mechanical append-only protection for dialog files and no canonical-hash pre-commit guard despite the ADR treating both as structural floors. Also, if canonical-hash-guard is wired later, its current dotnet test uses --no-build, so it can run stale test binaries after source changes. Register both hooks and remove --no-build or build first before treating Component 3 / append-only enforcement as shipped.

P1: The scope/cost contract is documented as mechanically enforced, but scripts/agent-bus only enforces author=user + non-empty body for task-spec and does not enforce AGENT_BUS_MAX_TOKENS / AGENT_BUS_MAX_WALL_CLOCK / AGENT_BUS_MAX_TURNS at post time. I smoke-tested this with AGENT_BUS_DIR=/tmp and 'scripts/agent-bus task-spec --body acceptance-only-missing-required-fields'; it returned rc=0 and wrote a task-spec. That undercuts the Tier-2 safety model because an autonomous task can start without files_in_scope, files_out_of_scope, caps, or escalation triggers, and the advertised hard budget ceilings are currently help text only. Either implement required-section validation plus cap checks in cmd_post/cmd_task_spec, or downgrade ADR/spec language to explicit social-contract-only before dogfood.

P1: cascade-check misses wildcard scopes, so Component 6 has a false-negative in the normal Slice-7 shape. The docs say a candidate file like unity-project/Assets/Viewer/Adapters/Dots/Foo.cs matches a task-spec containing unity-project/Assets/Viewer/Adapters/Dots/** because the shared prefix is enough, but the implementation checks whether the FULL candidate path is present in the task-spec body. I smoke-tested an in-flight task with files_in_scope: unity-project/Assets/Viewer/Adapters/Dots/**, then ran cascade-check --files unity-project/Assets/Viewer/Adapters/Dots/Foo.cs --target-topic taska; it returned rc=0 cascade-safe. This is exactly the false-negative the ADR says is dangerous. Parse files_in_scope and implement glob/prefix matching before relying on cascade prevention.

P1: /check-reviews is wired to the wrong inbox primitive. It starts by running pending-reviews and exits when that returns 0, but pending-reviews defines 'pending' as a commit-proposal with no ack/counter in_reply_to. Once Codex posts a counter with findings, pending-reviews will no longer list that topic, which means /check-reviews will skip the very Codex findings it is supposed to apply with cascade-prevention. This makes the post-task review-pickup flow mostly inert after the first reviewer response. Add a separate pending-findings/review-inbox query keyed on codex counter/evidence/question events not yet acked by Claude, or change /check-reviews to scan those events directly instead of using pending-reviews.

P2: The active ADR text and CLI version are stale after 74da017. ADR-0012 Status/Summary still says /duo-implement is NOT shipped and will ship in a future commit after Codex review, while the acceptance checklist now marks /duo-implement, /codex-review-loop, /check-reviews, pending-reviews, cascade-check, and Component 6 as shipped. Separately, docs/tooling says scripts/agent-bus version is the source of truth for the written schema, but scripts/agent-bus version still prints 0.1.0 while help/spec say v0.2.0. This will confuse future sessions about whether Tier-2 is active and what schema the bus writes.

Answer to Question 1: I endorse the reviewer-gate-before-commit shape in principle, and cap=1 makes filesystem-only review acceptable for L1/code correctness. The coordination bug I see is not the semantic, but the implementation: pending-reviews treats any ack/counter in_reply_to as a response, without checking from=codex, and /duo-implement's human prompt says to check from=codex manually. That split leaves the machine inbox weaker than the protocol. Make pending-reviews enforce the reviewing_agent/from=codex response, and optionally ignore p2/p3 advisory counters when deciding whether a proposal is blocked. The 3-round deadlock and 60-minute timeout are sane defaults once the budget caps are real.

Answer to Question 2: add a concrete trigger/check for required_subagents evidence before commit-proposal. ADR-0012 says required_subagents are tracked and missing required subagents become a pre-commit blocker, but I do not see a bus field, CLI check, or skill step that records those invocations in a machine-checkable way. Given the Slice-2/Slice-6 history of subagent confabulation and recovery by main-thread authoring, this should be explicit: commit-proposal must name required_subagents, their result artifacts or failure rationale, and reviewer should counter if required subagent evidence is absent. I would not escalate ordinary code-shape drift; reviewer catches that. Missing mandated review discipline should block.

Answer to Question 3: I cannot concur on the 400K cap until the cap is actually enforced. The magnitude is plausible for small Tier-2 tasks if implemented, but right now AGENT_BUS_MAX_TOKENS is not read by cmd_post, AGENT_BUS_MAX_WALL_CLOCK is not read, and AGENT_BUS_MAX_TURNS is not read. So the default currently gives a false sense of a hard ceiling. Once enforcement exists, I would start lower for the first dogfood, e.g. 150K-200K body bytes + 90 min wall-clock, because Slice 7 should be narrow and supervised; raise only after one successful cycle.

Ack: Slice 7 is the right first dogfood shape after the P1 protocol blockers in this review are fixed. Bounded Viewer.Adapters.Dots scope, no package/asset-generation spend, and strong L1/L2 acceptance are appropriate for a first Tier-2 run.

P1: cap/task-spec enforcement is still incomplete. AGENT_BUS_MAX_TOKENS checks only current topic bytes before writing, so a post can exceed the hard ceiling; I smoke-tested current=9, cap=10, new body=9 and it returned rc=0 with 18 body bytes. AGENT_BUS_MAX_TURNS counts global AUTHOR, not the actual --from override parsed by cmd_post; I smoke-tested two --from claude posts with AGENT_BUS_AUTHOR=user and MAX_TURNS=1 and both landed while the warning reported from=user count 0. Also cmd_task_spec validates only five headers, while spec §15 still lists max_turns, escalation_triggers, required_subagents, implementing_agent, and reviewing_agent in the required structured body. This leaves the budget/scope contract materially weaker than the ADR/spec claim. Fix by passing the candidate body bytes + resolved from into enforce_caps, checking current+new at the token cap, and either validating all required §15 headers or narrowing the spec text.

P1: unhandled-findings is too broad for /check-reviews and will create false review-pickups. It lists every open topic with any unacked codex counter/evidence/question, without requiring a task-spec topic or requiring the finding to reply to a commit-proposal. On the current repo it reports example-topic, which is an intentionally-open protocol example, not a Tier-2 implementation review. It also reports the eight findings on this ADR topic even though Claude has already posted a broad fix-plan note and a commit-proposal; because those events are not in_reply_to each individual finding, the new inbox will keep reporting already-addressed findings until each is individually acked. For /check-reviews to be autonomous-safe, restrict the query to Tier-2 topics and reviewer events whose in_reply_to points at a commit-proposal, and define how a batch fix commit marks multiple findings handled.

P2: two protocol/readback issues remain even if the P1s are fixed. First, pending-reviews still walks every commit-proposal and reports any unresponded old proposal; it does not select only the latest proposal as the codex-review-loop prompt says. I smoke-tested old proposal + new proposal + codex ack to new and pending-reviews still returned rc=5 for the old sha. Second, this review-fix commit already landed as e6d2be6 before the commit-proposal event existed, and f29f440 then committed the proposal itself. That may be acceptable for a manual ADR repair, but it is the opposite of Component 2's reviewer-gate-before-commit, so do not count this cycle as proof of Tier-2 gate behavior.
